question: Explain sampling risk and non-sampling risk, the difference between statistical and non-statistical sampling, and how the auditor evaluates the results of a sample under SA 530.

points.label: Meaning of audit sampling
points.description: Applying audit procedures to less than 100% of items within a population so that all sampling units have a chance of selection, to provide a reasonable basis for conclusions about the whole population.

points.label: Sampling risk and non-sampling risk
points.description: Sampling risk is the risk that the auditor's conclusion from a sample may differ from the conclusion if the whole population were tested; non-sampling risk arises from factors unrelated to sample size, such as wrong procedures or misinterpreting evidence.
points.basis: SA 530, definitions of sampling risk and non-sampling risk

points.label: Statistical vs non-statistical sampling
points.description: Statistical sampling uses random selection and probability theory to evaluate results and measure sampling risk; otherwise the approach is non-statistical.

points.label: Tolerable misstatement and sample design
points.description: Determine sample size, considering tolerable misstatement, the expected misstatement and the population characteristics, so that sampling risk is reduced to an acceptably low level.
points.basis: SA 530, sample design, size and selection of items for testing

points.label: Evaluating results and projecting misstatements
points.description: Project misstatements found in the sample to the population, investigate the nature and cause of deviations, and evaluate whether the sample provides a reasonable basis for conclusions.
points.basis: SA 530, nature and cause of deviations and misstatements, projecting misstatements and evaluating results
